title: Circle Theorems: Angles, Chords, Tangents and Secants
standard_text: G.12A apply theorems about circles, including relationships among angles, radii, chords, tangents, and secants, to solve non-contextual problems
meta_desc: Free Geometry circle worksheets for Texas TEKS G.12A: central and inscribed angles, inscribed quadrilaterals, tangents, chords and secants. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A central angle equals its arc. An inscribed angle is half its arc.
  • Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to 180°.
  • A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency. Two tangents from one point are congruent.
  • Angles formed by chords and secants use half the sum or half the difference of the arcs.

Examples

Example

Inscribed angle on a 124° arc

half of 124

Answer: 62°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the whole arc for an inscribed angleTake half.
Opposite angles adding to 360°They add to 180°.
Forgetting the right angleRadius ⊥ tangent.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 12 and PA = 16. Find OP.
items.e: OA ⟂ PA, so OP is the hypotenuse: √(12² + 16²) = 20.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = 3x + 9 and PB = 6x − 9. Find PA.
items.e: Tangent segments from one point are congruent: 3x + 9 = 6x − 9, so 3x = 18 and x = 6. PA = 27.

items.q: PA is tangent to circle O at A. OA = 3 and OP = 5. Find PA.
items.e: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so △OAP is a right triangle with hypotenuse OP. PA = √(5² − 3²) = 4.

items.q: PA and PB are tangent to circle O. PA = 22. Find PB.

items.q: Two inscribed angles intercept the same arc. How are they related?
items.e: Each is half of the same arc, so they are equal. They are congruent.

items.q: Two secants meet outside a circle. The far arc is 174° and the near arc is 52°. Find the angle between the secants.
items.e: An angle outside the circle is half the difference of the intercepted arcs: (174° − 52°) ÷ 2 = 61°.

items.q: Two chords intersect inside a circle. The arcs intercepted by the angle and its vertical angle measure 70° and 44°. Find the angle.
items.e: An angle formed by two chords is half the sum of the intercepted arcs: (70° + 44°) ÷ 2 = 57°.

items.q: Which quadrilateral can always be inscribed in a circle?

items.q: A central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc. The central angle is 110°. What is the inscribed angle?
